text:
sam: Heads up — seeing weird failures in us-west-2. Interface endpoint (vpce-0a1b2c3d) to partner svc is flapping, ALB target group health checks to our internal app are intermittently failing with 502/504. Pods that hit the partner via PrivateLink time out. Anyone seen this pattern?

maria: Can you paste the endpoint ENI + route table + endpoint SG? Also which subnets the app pods run in.

vikram: grabbing outputs — pasting sanitized snippets.

vikram: ```
$ aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0f12345abcde
{
  "NetworkInterfaces": [
    {
      "NetworkInterfaceId": "eni-0f12345abcde",
      "SubnetId": "subnet-0aaa1111",
      "PrivateIpAddress": "10.0.45.12",
      "Groups": [ { "GroupId": "sg-0bbcc22" } ]
    }
  ]
}
```

vikram: route table for subnet-0aaa1111 shows 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0xdeadbeef and no explicit route to the endpoint (interface endpoints use DNS to resolve to the ENI IPs).

sam: Verified with tcpdump on a node — SYN to endpoint IP leaves, SYN-ACK comes back to nat EIP, not pod IP. So return path looks SNAT'd. Snippet:

sam: ```
09:12:03.123456 IP 10.0.50.11.39352 > 10.0.45.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0
09:12:03.123578 IP 198.51.100.23.443 > 203.0.113.5.39352: Flags [S.], seq 0
```

sam: The 198.51.100.23 is our NAT EIP — looks like something is forcing traffic via NAT (source IP rewritten) before it reaches the endpoint, so endpoint SG is rejecting or the partner sees unexpected source.

julia: Do we have a transparent proxy/iptables REDIRECT in nodes? Last week we enabled a cluster-wide HTTP proxy for egress and used iptables to intercept 443 for certain domains. If that proxy sends upstream via NAT, that would SNAT the flows.

maria: Check iptables on node: `sudo iptables -t nat -S` — any REDIRECT or DNAT rules?

vikram: I grabbed that too:

vikram: ```
$ sudo iptables -t nat -S
-P PREROUTING ACCEPT
-P INPUT ACCEPT
-P OUTPUT ACCEPT
-P POSTROUTING ACCEPT
-N PROXY_REDIRECT
-A PREROUTING -p tcp --dport 443 -m owner --uid-owner 210 -j PROXY_REDIRECT
-A PROXY_REDIRECT -p tcp -j REDIRECT --to-ports 15001
-A POSTROUTING -s 10.0.0.0/16 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```

vikram: The MASQUERADE on POSTROUTING plus the redirect means intercepted traffic is SNAT'd when it leaves via eth0. That explains NAT EIP showing up.

maria: OK that matches. Interface endpoint SG (sg-0bbcc22) only had cluster CIDR allowed (10.0.0.0/16). Because traffic is SNAT'd to the NAT EIP, the ENI sees source=nat EIP and denies it. The flapping happens when some requests bypass the proxy (direct DNS -> ENI) and others get redirected -> SNAT -> dropped by endpoint SG.

sam: Reproduced by curling the partner domain with/without the proxy:

sam: ```
$ curl -v https://partner.example.internal/health --connect-timeout 3
* Connected to 10.0.45.12 (10.0.45.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake... then timeout (when proxied)
```

julia: Quick mitigation options: 1) Update endpoint SG to allow NAT EIP (ugly but fast). 2) Bypass iptables redirect for partner domains so traffic goes straight to ENI and preserves pod source IP (preferred). 3) Use a proxy that preserves original src (e.g., TPROXY + routing) but that's more work.

maria: Agreed. For immediate relief I added NAT EIP + cluster CIDR to sg-0bbcc22 so both direct and SNAT'd traffic are allowed. Also patched node iptables to exclude partner domains from the PREROUTING redirect (added ipset check).

sam: After that ALB health checks stabilized within ~2m and partner calls stopped timing out. We'll put a task in infra backlog to remove IP-based allowances and fix the proxy behavior.

vikram: Filing follow-up: infra#1245 to audit all interface endpoints for SGs that reference IPs instead of security-group refs / prefix-lists.

julia: FYI deploy-bot shows the rollback window expired during the flapping, no real user impact but noisy alerts.

deploy-bot: Incident note: automated alert triggered (vpce-0a1b2c3d) 09:10 — resolved 09:18 after SG update.

sam: Thanks all. Plan: keep NAT-EIP allowance for 24h, then remove once proxy exclusion is confirmed across nodes. :thumbsup:
